title: Diagram Studio spec
description: A declarative grid diagram: nodes sit in grid cells (so they never overlap), edges run only through the gutters between rows and columns (so they never cross a node). Rendered and lint-checked by diagram.js — see https://diagram-studio.bibas.dev/diagram.js and /agents.md for the full guide. additionalProperties is true everywhere: the engine ignores fields it does not know, so an unrecognized field is silently dropped rather than rejected — but only the fields documented here do anything.

title.description: Diagram title. Used as the SVG's accessible name (aria-label/<title>) and, by dgs render --format html, the page <title>. Not drawn on the canvas itself.

scale.description: "doc" for an inline document figure (≤ ~1072px wide, ≤4 columns recommended). "slide" for a 1920x1080 deck slide (bigger type, wider canvas). This is also where a share link (#s=/#j=) and dgs's wrapper input ({"scale":...,"spec":...}) carry the scale — as this same field, inside the spec.

flow.description: Direction auto-placement lays out nodes that have no col/row: layers stack downward (rows grow) by default, or rightward (columns grow) with "right". Only affects nodes missing col/row; nodes with both are never moved.

interactive.description: When true, every node is focusable and clickable; clicking (or Enter/Space when focused) fires a "diagram:select" CustomEvent on the figure with detail = the node object.

nodes.description: The boxes. Order does not affect layout but does affect auto-placement tie-breaks and z-order.

edges.description: Arrows between nodes, always routed through row/column gutters.

groups.description: Zones: a dashed rectangle with a two-line header (label + caption) drawn behind a rectangular block of cells, or behind a named set of nodes.

id.description: Unique within the spec. Referenced by edges' from/to and groups' nodes.

label.description: Node title. Wraps to two lines, then shrinks to fit, then the render lint flags it — keep it to roughly 24 characters or less so it never has to.

sub.description: A smaller caption line under the label (e.g. a tech detail or metric). Keep it to roughly 28 characters or less.

col.description: Zero-based grid column. Omit BOTH col and row to have the node auto-placed; giving only one is invalid — either give both, for a precise layout, or neither.

colspan.description: How many columns wide the node spans, starting at col.

kind.description: Visual role. "hot" is the accent fill and marks the ONE thing the diagram is about — use at most one per diagram, everywhere else on the highlighted path use "key" (an ink outline). "db" draws a cylinder. "store"/"term" draw a pill (term is muted). "ext" is dashed, for systems outside the one being diagrammed. "bad" and "muted" are self-explanatory.

icon.description: One glyph drawn before the label. Also printable with `dgs icons`.

children.description: Turns the node into a container: the title moves to the top-left and these render as a row of child boxes inside it. A container is taller than a plain node.

label.description: Child box text; wraps and shrinks like a node label.

kind.description: Only "hot" and "key" are styled on a child box; other values are accepted but drawn plain.

step.description: Build-step marker for a slide deck: adds class "step" and data-step=<value>, so a slide framework can reveal it incrementally. Any scalar value.

label.description: Text on the edge. Keep it to 1-3 words — it sizes the column gap between horizontally adjacent nodes and wraps to at most two lines.

hot.description: Heavier stroke, in the accent/ink highlight colour — marks the ONE path the diagram is about, alongside "key" nodes.

via.description: Which gutter a long edge (same column, far rows; or same row, far columns) should route through, when the default choice crosses something.

both.description: Draw an arrowhead at both ends.

exit.description: Force which side of the FROM node the edge leaves from.

enter.description: Force which side of the TO node the edge arrives at.

group.description: Either give "nodes" (the zone wraps exactly those nodes' cells — simplest, and safe if the layout changes), or give both "rows" and "cols" (a fixed rectangular block of cells; every other node whose cell falls inside it is flagged by the render lint, so either add it to the zone or move it out).

label.description: Zone title, shown top-left of the zone.

nodes.description: Node ids the zone wraps. Mutually exclusive with rows/cols.

rows.description: [firstRow, lastRow], inclusive, firstRow ≤ lastRow. Requires "cols" too.

cols.description: [firstCol, lastCol], inclusive, firstCol ≤ lastCol. Requires "rows" too.
